newsitem.title: USA: U.S. ship off Zaire ready to help rescue Americans.
newsitem.headline: U.S. ship off Zaire ready to help rescue Americans.

text.p: The U.S. Navy helicopter ship Nassau was in position off the west coast of Africa, ready to help in the evacuation of Americans from Zaire if required, the Defence Department said on Thursday.

"We are there in case an evacuation is necessary," Pentagon spokesman Ken Bacon told reporters. "The USS Nassau is currently on station about 220 miles (354 km) off the coast of Africa, about the confluence of Congo, Zaire and Angola."

He said that the Nassau, with nearly 1,400 Marines aboard, could move closer if necessary but stressed that there had been no request from the U.S. Embassy in the capital of Kinshasa for a rescue operation.
Defence officials said that there were believed to be more than 500 Americans in Zaire, including some 470 private citizens.
"We are hopeful that peace talks will, in fact, begin over the next couple of days and there will be a peaceful solution to the problem," Bacon said.
He said that a detachment of Marines had moved into Brazzaville, the capital of the Congo, near Kinshasa to coordinate a rescue operation if necessary.
At the State Department, spokesman Nicholas Burns pressed the U.S. call for increased access by relief workers to some 100,000 Rwandan refugees staying south of the rebel-held city of Kisangani.
U.S. diplomats have been discussing the situation with representatives of rebel leader Laurent Kabila, Burns said.
Asked why Kabila's forces might balk at granting access to the refugees, Burns said, "I believe that the rebel alliance is concerned about security issues."
But he added, "Frankly, the rebel alliance has a humanitarian obligation to help tens of thousands Rwandan refugees who have been caught in the midst of this fighting."
